items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: You could never buy the Eiffel Tower. In nineteen twenty-five, one man lost a fortune trying. Why did he stay silent?
The tower was only meant to stand twenty years. By nineteen twenty-five, it was rusting and costly.
So con man Victor Lustig got fake government letterhead, and invited scrap dealers to a luxury hotel.
His pitch: the state will sell the tower for scrap. Top secret.
But wouldn't the buyer just go to the police?
Dealer André Poisson paid, plus a bribe, and Lustig vanished with the cash.
And that's not even the craziest part.
Poisson was too embarrassed to report it. So Lustig came back, and tried to sell it again.
He never sold a tower. He sold the buyer's silence.
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched banknote, worried] Is the Taj Mahal still available?
Comment: would you have told the police?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
